name: Loktak Lake
description: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India and a Ramsar site, famous for its unique floating phumdis (heterogeneous masses of vegetation, soil and organic matter). Located in Bishnupur district about 48 km south of Imphal; home to the world’s only floating national park and traditional lake communities.
facts: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India
Ramsar wetland designated 2002
Famous for floating phumdis
About 48 km south of Imphal in Bishnupur district
Surface elevation around 768 m

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: World’s only floating national park, located on the largest phumdi in the southeastern part of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district. Last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer or dancing deer). Accessed by boat; a unique wetland ecosystem for wildlife viewing.
facts: World’s only floating national park
Last habitat of the Sangai deer (Rucervus eldii eldii)
Established 1977; area about 40 km²
On southeastern shore of Loktak Lake
Accessed primarily by boat from Sendra or Keibul

name: INA Martyrs' Memorial Complex (Moirang)
description: Historic site in Moirang town, Bishnupur district, where the Indian National Army first hoisted the Indian tricolour on Indian soil on 14 April 1944 under Colonel Shaukat Malik. Complex includes museum with INA relics, photographs and documents related to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s campaign.
facts: First INA flag hoisting on Indian soil, 14 April 1944
Located in Moirang, about 45 km from Imphal
Houses INA War Museum with artefacts
Part of the 1944 Imphal-Kohima campaign history
Official tourist place of Bishnupur district

name: Bishnupur Vishnu Temple
description: 15th-century brick temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Bishnupur town, from which the district derives its name. Built by King Kyamba after receiving a Vishnu idol; protected monument with distinctive conical/corbelled architecture blending local and external influences.
facts: Built in 15th century during reign of King Kyamba
District HQ named after this temple (Bishnupur = abode of Vishnu)
Protected historical monument under ASI
About 27 km from Imphal on Tiddim Road
Unique brick and lime construction

name: Red Hill (Maibam Lotpa Ching / Lokpaching)
description: WWII battlefield site on a hillock about 17 km south of Imphal in Bishnupur district on Tiddim Road. Site of fierce fighting in the Battle of Imphal (1944) between Allied and Japanese forces; features India Peace Memorial and war cemetery for Japanese soldiers.
facts: Site of decisive 1944 Battle of Imphal fighting
India Peace Memorial constructed by Japanese veterans
About 17 km south of Imphal on NH-150
Also known as Maibam Lotpa Ching or Lokpaching
Imphal Peace Museum nearby with war relics

name: Sendra Island
description: Rocky hillock island in the middle of Loktak Lake offering panoramic views of the floating phumdis and lake expanse. Connected by causeway; hosts tourist bungalow and is a popular base for boating to Keibul Lamjao and photography of the wetland.
facts: Hillock island in central Loktak Lake
Best panoramic views of phumdis
Sendra Tourist Home / resort on the island
About 48–50 km from Imphal
Gateway for boat trips to Keibul Lamjao

name: Phubala
description: Charming resort and lakeside spot on the western fringes of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district, about 40 km south of Imphal. Offers serene views, boating and a quieter alternative for experiencing the wetland landscape.
facts: On western fringes of Loktak Lake
About 40 km from Imphal
Popular for lakeside stays and views
Official tourist place of Bishnupur
Quieter alternative to main Sendra area

name: Loukoipat Ecological Park
description: Ecological park and small lake area on the outskirts of Bishnupur town near Tiddim Road. Developed for nature walks, picnics and local recreation amid greenery; a favourite short-stop tourist spot in the district.
facts: Near Bishnupur district headquarters
On outskirts along Tiddim Road / NH-150
Boating and scenic picnic facilities
Official tourist place listed by district
Developed ecological and recreational site

name: Moirang
description: Historic town in Bishnupur district on the fringe of Loktak Lake, sacred in Meitei tradition and site of the first INA flag hoisting. Gateway to the lake circuit, with cultural significance linked to Lai Haraoba and local temples.
facts: About 45 km from Imphal
Site of first INA tricolour hoisting in 1944
Sacred place in Meitei tradition
Base for Loktak Lake and Keibul visits
Headquarters area for southern Bishnupur tourism

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall
description: Picturesque multi-tiered waterfall site about 20 km from Imphal beside Tiddim Road near the Bishnupur–Senapati border area. Perennial falls in a scenic foothill setting; a relatively newer tourist spot for short nature visits.
facts: About 20 km from Imphal on NH-150
Three waterfalls in scenic setting
Officially listed among Bishnupur tourist places
On possible Bishnupur-Senapati border
Perennial and accessible for day visits
